events.title: Visiting Tan Ah Tah Professorial Lecture - False Friend: The Frailties and Pathologies of Alliances
events.venue: Yale-NUS Hall, University Town (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: Modern geopolitics has thrown the question of alliances into sharp relief. We habitually valorise alliances as guarantees of security and friendship, binding states into a shared future. Yet alliances also harbour pathologies: they can drag states into war, suffer from a credible-commitment problem, and vary in equality. The lecture pursues Montesquieu’s intuition that alliances must be seen as just to bind; when one party commands and the other complies, trust erodes and costly power follows.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Senior Counsel Forum 2026 - Module 3: Disciplinary Process and Disciplinary Cases: Don’t Get Charged
events.outline: The Senior Counsel Forum, by the Law Society of Singapore, returns with six modules led by distinguished Senior Counsel. Topics include court submissions, duty to the court, disciplinary processes, conflicts of interest, common ethical scenarios, and English ethics practice. An invaluable opportunity for lawyers to learn best practices in legal ethics, delivered virtually via Zoom.

events.title: NUS Faculty of Law Graduate Programmes and Auditing Programme AY2026/2027 Semester 1+
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: Event Link

events.title: [WEBINAR] Community Law Training Programme 2026 - Module 7: Mental Capacity Matters, Wills & Probate
events.outline: This module focuses on the practical issues encountered when advising clients on mental capacity, estate planning and post-death matters in community, pro bono and low-bono settings. The session covers situations involving persons who lack mental capacity, including deputyship applications, as well as common challenges faced when managing wills and probate matters for vulnerable clients and families.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Building a Professional Brand and Delivering an Impactful Pitch for Legal Professionals (Session 2)
events.outline: This exclusive three-part webinar series is designed to equip legal professionals with the tools, mindset, and strategies to build a compelling personal brand, show up authentically in every interaction, and deliver pitches that win mandates and open doors.

events.title: PIPEs: Applying the Magic of Mediation to IP Disputes: Commercial Outcomes & Ethical Considerations
events.outline:
With the growing complexity and increasing number of international commercial disputes, including in the field of IP and technology, how has mediation floated up as an unlikely dark horse in providing a potentially effective dispute resolution process? 
Join us for a deep dive session exploring practical issues in mediation from the perspectives of disputants, legal counsel and mediator.

events.title: [WEBINAR] People, Pitfalls, and Practice: Managing Interpersonal Challenges in Law
events.outline: In this webinar, participants will learn why challenging behaviors arise, gain greater awareness of their own triggers and default responses, and learn practical strategies to navigate difficult conversations with colleagues, supervisors, and clients.

events.title: [WEBINAR] E154: Anti-Money Laundering / Combating The Financing Of Terrorism (“AML / CFT”) Course
events.outline: This event is organised by Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (ISCA). The course is designed to enable RFAs to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of AML/CFT legislations, regulatory trends and developments in Singapore, knowledge and understanding of the AML/CFT environment in Singapore and international trends and typologies, knowledge and understanding of how to carry out risk assessment and conduct various types of customer due diligence, familiarity with ACRA Guidelines for RFAs and awareness of how ACRA’s Compliance review and inspections impact RFAs.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 7: Demystifying DNA: Understanding Forensic DNA Evidence in Criminal Defence
events.outline:
How is DNA extracted, analysed, and used in court? In this seminar, forensic experts break down the science behind DNA profiling—from hair, bodily fluids, and beyond—and explain how this evidence can shape legal outcomes.
Gain practical insights into lab processes, interpreting DNA reports, and how to effectively work with forensic experts in criminal cases.

events.title: Privacy and Data Protection Law in Singapore
events.outline: This is the book launch of Privacy and Data Protection Law in Singapore. Alongside the book launch, there will be a seminar and panel discussion about the boundaries of privacy law in Singapore.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Large Firms – Business Planning, Marketing and Client Development
events.venue: Organiser The Law Society of Singapore
events.outline: Large law firms must balance growth, client expectations, and internal alignment. This session, combining College of Law Australia's practice management expertise with Singapore practitioner insights, explores aligning strategic plans with practice priorities, targeted marketing, and client development. It examines strengthening client relationships, addressing complex needs, and enhancing market positioning, viewed through Singapore's evolving legal landscape, offering practical strategies for scaling sustainably while preserving quality and trust.

events.title: [WEBINAR] International Arbitration In Practice 2026 - Session 3: Working with Third Parties: Co-counsel and Experts
events.outline: This session explores practical considerations in managing relationships with local counsel, foreign lawyers, barristers, and expert witnesses in international arbitration. Drawing on practitioners’ experiences, it examines cross-jurisdictional challenges, common pitfalls, and effective strategies. The session also covers engaging and instructing experts, including expert briefs, timelines, independence, conflicts of interest, and preparing useful expert evidence for international tribunals.

events.title: Lunchtime Conversations: Redesigning Legal Work for the Future
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This seminar is targeted at managing partners, general counsel, team leaders and HR professionals in law firms and in-house legal teams.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 8: Criminal Defence in the Digital Age: Harnessing AI & Digital Forensics
events.outline:
Digital forensics and AI are reshaping the legal landscape—how should criminal defence lawyers adapt?
Join us for a forward-looking webinar exploring how cutting-edge tools like predictive analytics, legal AI (including ChatGPT), and digital forensics are transforming criminal defence work.

events.title: [WEBINAR] AI Meets ESG: What Legal Professionals Need to Know
events.outline: AI governance and ESG are converging rapidly, creating new legal risks, regulatory expectations and business opportunities. This webinar brings together regulators, governance experts and lawyers to examine how AI-ESG integration is reshaping corporate governance, sustainability reporting, carbon markets, digital infrastructure and disputes. Participants will gain practical insights into governance, regulatory compliance, contractual risk allocation and emerging liability issues.

events.title: JLP - Translating Corporate Governance Principles into Legal Frameworks
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: This module is designed to equip junior lawyers with the skills to advise clients on corporate governance issues, and how to balance ethical considerations with the rights of relevant stakeholders, and to comply with the prevailing regulations.

events.title: SMU Yong Pung How School of Law Auditing Programme AY2026-27 Term 1+
events.outline: SMU Yong Pung How School of Law is pleased to invite members of the legal fraternity in Singapore and other interested parties to apply to audit selected LLB courses offered by the school. Participants are welcome to attend and observe seminars taught by our instructors. They are exempted from course requirements and a certificate of attendance will be awarded at the end of the course upon meeting the attendance requirements.

events.title: Visiting Sat Pal Khattar Professorial Lecture - The Insurance Act 2015: Is the Devil in the Detail?
events.venue: Yale-NUS Hall, University Town (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: The Insurance Act 2015 introduced significant changes to insurance contract law, amending or repealing central provisions of the Marine Insurance Act 1906. In force since August 2016, it marks its tenth anniversary this August. The reforms are broadly welcome, but questions remain about consistency within insurance contract law, consistency with general contract law, and the optimal level of legislative detail.

events.title: China, Hong Kong & Asia: The New Capital Markets and M&A Order
events.venue: RHTLaw Asia LLP, 16 Collyer Quay #08-00, Collyer Quay Centre, Singapore 049318
events.outline: This event is organised by RHT Academy Pte. Ltd. As Asia becomes the centre of global capital flows and investment, this session explores the legal and regulatory developments shaping cross-border capital markets and M&A across China, Hong Kong and ASEAN. Participants will gain practical insights into transaction structuring, regulatory approvals, due diligence, compliance, ESG, digital assets, and strategies for navigating an increasingly Asia-centric dealmaking environment.

events.title: CIL’s Dialogue with Republic of South Africa’s High Commissioner Charlotte Lobe
events.venue: NUS Bukit Timah Campus, Seminar Room 4-4, Block B Level 4, 469 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore 259756
events.outline: This event is organised by NUS Centre for International Law. Talk by Republic of South Africa’s High Commissioner Charlotte Lobe on South Africa’s role in taking Israel to the ICJ on the allegation that it is committing genocide against the Palestinians in Gaza.

events.title: Prompt to Practice: A Launchpad for Exploring AI in Legal Work
events.venue: Members' Lounge (The Law Society of Singapore), 28 Maxwell Road, #01-03, Singapore 069120
events.outline: This hands-on workshop is designed for lawyers who are beginning to explore AI and want a practical, grounded introduction to what it can do for their practice.

events.title: JLP - Application Advocacy+
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: Get equipped with essential skills to effectively prepare for and argue applications in court.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Community Law Training Programme 2026 - Module 8: Child Protection Proceedings
events.outline:
Child Protection Proceedings can be complex, urgent, and deeply impactful. Using a practical overview of how Care and Protection Order applications are handled in the Youth Court, and the role counsel can play in supporting families through the process.
Learn the key stages of proceedings, from first mention to social report hearings, family conferences, contested hearings, and appeals. Gain insight into common court orders, expectations of represented parties, and how legal assistance can help clients navigate emotionally charged situations with clarity and confidence.

events.title: [WEBINAR] AML/CFT/PF in Practice: Managing Client Risk, Red Flags and Reporting Obligations in Today’s Legal Landscape
events.outline: By the end of the programme, participants should be able to identify key AML/CFT/PF risks in legal practice, recognise common and emerging red flags, assess when enhanced due diligence or ongoing monitoring may be required, understand the practical considerations around STR filing, and appreciate the importance of proper documentation, internal controls and escalation within the law practice.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 9: Drug Offences & Forensics: What Defence Counsels Need to Know
events.outline: Understanding how drugs metabolise in the body can make or break a defence. This seminar equips criminal defence lawyers with essential knowledge on drug pathways, forensic testing, and interpreting HSA reports.

events.title: AI Workshop for Legal Professionals (20 August 2026)
events.venue: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, 7 Raffles Ave., Marina Bay, Singapore 039799
events.outline: Step into the world of artificial intelligence with this practical, in-person workshop designed specifically for legal professionals. Gain foundational skills and the confidence to apply AI in your everyday work—from legal research to drafting and contract analysis. Guided by experienced trainers, you'll explore how to evaluate and use a range of general and legal-specific AI tools effectively and responsibly. Participants will work directly on their own devices with live support, ensuring a hands-on, outcome-focused learning experience.

events.title: The PIPD 2026 Seminar
events.outline: The PIPD Seminar 2026 addresses the evolving landscape of personal injury and property damage practice across five sessions — covering dependency and inheritance claims, the ethical obligations and guardrails governing AI adoption in legal practice, AI-generated quantum submissions, the paradigm shift in motor vehicle accident reconstruction, and a panel discussion on precedent cases shaping PIPD law in Singapore.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Sustainability Apex Programme Masterclass #10: ESG Tech and Data
events.outline: This masterclass provides an overview of ESG technology and data, examining how ESG data is collected, governed, and integrated to support sustainability reporting, assurance readiness, and decarbonisation efforts. It highlights key technology trends and governance considerations relevant to lawyers and compliance professionals advising on ESG disclosures, controls, and accountability.

events.title: Certificate in Wealth, Succession and Legacy
events.outline: This event is organised by Wealth Management Institute Limited. This course provides an overview of the legal and practical considerations in wealth transition and succession planning. Participants examine how purpose and governance influence long-term family decisions, and review key estate-planning tools and structures. The module also explores philanthropic planning and the role of legal practitioners in supporting families through legacy, governance, and wealth-planning discussions.

events.title: [CALS] Stephen Brogan-Jones Day Legal Fellowship Lecture on the Rule of Law on Defensive Democracy: Assessing Taiwan’s Democratic Self-Defense Framework
events.venue: Yale-NUS Hall, Faculty of Law, University Town
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: Defensive democracy, developed by Karl Loewenstein after witnessing the rise of Hitler, holds that democracies may restrict anti-democratic forces from using democratic freedoms to destroy democracy itself. Germany adopts a militant model, while the United States permits restrictions only when there is a clear and present danger. Taiwan has adopted a middle-ground approach, and debate continues over whether it should strengthen its defensive measures.

events.title: Self-Leadership for Lawyers: Taking Charge of your Work Life - Module 1
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This session will introduce Mindful Business Singapore’s Lawyers’ Sustainability Report with the main focus being on its section on personal wellbeing for lawyers, to build Participants’ awareness of our human needs for thriving and developing greater awareness of their personal capacity to sustain their wellbeing and effectiveness.

events.title: [WEBINAR] International Arbitration In Practice 2026 - Session 4: Global Enforcement Strategies
events.outline: This session examines strategies for enforcing arbitral awards across Asia and against sovereign states. It explores procedural hurdles, sovereign immunity, investor-state enforcement challenges, and practical approaches to recovery. Participants will also gain insights into global asset tracing, cross-border enforcement coordination, forensic tools, freezing injunctions, disclosure orders, and other mechanisms used to identify and secure assets before they dissipate.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Recent Developments in Family Law – Legislative Reforms and Therapeutic Justice in Singapore
events.outline: There have been many significant changes to Family Law legislation in recent years. This seminar seeks to provide an overview of the key changes, including the sixth fact relating to divorce, the new regimes and frameworks relating to enforcement of custody and access orders, maintenance enforcement, and the enhanced judge-led powers of the court. The speakers will also review the effectiveness of these changes in strengthening Therapeutic Justice elements in our family proceedings.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Converging or Diverging? New Developments in the Regulation of Digital Assets across the EU, Singapore, and the United States
events.outline: This webinar examines the rapid consolidation of digital asset frameworks in the EU, Singapore, and the US. Moving beyond a basic jurisdiction survey, the session provides a comparative analysis of key developments, including the EU’s MiCA, Singapore’s stablecoin regime, and the US GENIUS and CLARITY Acts. Participants will gain a structured understanding of the changing legal landscape.

events.title: Family Law Masterclass for the Advanced Practitioner+
events.venue: Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) The Adelphi, 1 Coleman Street #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: The Masterclass deals with the breadth and depth of family matters. While the standard topics such as matrimonial and divorce proceedings, maintenance, adopt, maintenance, will be covered, their treatment will focus on complex issues that experienced family lawyers may encounter or are increasingly encountering in their practice, such as pre-nuptial agreements, co-mingling of assets and enforcement of foreign divorce orders. At the end of the course, participants will achieve a better understanding and appreciation for, and thus able to better handle, complex family matters. The course is targeted at family law practitioners with at least 5 years of family law practice experience.

events.title: [WEBINAR & IN-PERSON] What To Do When The Mediator Goes Rogue? – Standards and Accountability in Mediation Seminar
events.venue: Webinar / 137 Amoy Street, Far East Square, #03-06, Singapore 049965
events.outline: This event is organised by Sage Mediation Institute for Leadership Education. When mediators conduct themselves poorly, what can users and their advocates do to maintain user confidence in mediation practice. This seminar examines standards of professional mediation and explores the recourse available to parties who encounter unprofessional mediator behaviour. Expert panellists comprising practitioners and policymakers will discuss the need to strengthen safeguards and accountability frameworks to protect mediation users and uphold confidence in professional mediation.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Climate Change and Human Rights
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore, Centre for International Law (NUS CIL). This module examines the growing recognition of the link between climate change and human rights from both global and regional perspectives. It explores institutional developments, climate-related litigation, and evolving legal frameworks addressing the impacts of climate change on individuals and communities. The session will also consider the challenges climate change poses for present and future generations through a comparative and dynamic analysis.

events.title: Copyright in the Digital Age: Balancing Creativity, Innovation and Access
events.outline: As our digital world continues to shape our daily lives, AI and digital content likewise continues to shape legal principles and copyright law. Bringing together leading IP practitioners and legal tech advisors to explore critical fronts in AI, litigation, and copyright protections and enforcement, this event provides a balanced and forward-looking forum for understanding the legal, technological, and market-operational aspects of copyright protection in a rapidly changing digital landscape.

events.title: INSOL International Singapore Seminar
events.venue: Fairmont Singapore , Raffles City Convention Centre , Singapore 189560
events.outline: This event is organised by INSOL International (Asia) Ltd. Panels will cover regional and international restructuring and insolvency hot topics, including global restructuring trends, funding for turnarounds, trust-related insolvency issues, and law reform across Asia-Pacific. Discussions will also address ethical issues, professional judgment and accountability, pre-insolvency debtor in possession workouts, market uncertainty, and an interactive rapid-response Q&A challenge.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 1: Liquidation And Receivership+
events.outline: This module provides participants with knowledge on the different modes of winding up, and with a particular focus on court-ordered winding up. Participants will also learn the basics of personal bankruptcy and the administrative process to exit bankruptcy through a discharge and/or an annulment.

events.title: PLDG-CLT-EWBCLB-SMA-CMEP Book Launch: Medical Negligence and The Duty to Advise – Beyond Autonomy
events.venue: Yale-NUS College Performance Hall  NUS Law (UTown), Kent Ridge Campus
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: This book contends that an excessive focus on patient autonomy has distorted negligence principles, fostering uncertainty among healthcare professionals and undermining trust in doctor-patient relationships. It advocates for a shift from an individualistic, rights-based approach to negligence towards a relational perspective emphasizing agency and shared decision-making. Theoretical analysis highlights anomalies in duty of care, standard of care, causation, and damage.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Community Law Training Programme 2026 - Module 9: Adoption and Guardianship
events.outline:
Adoption and guardianship matters often arise in complex family and caregiving situations, particularly in community and pro bono settings where children may be cared for informally, family arrangements are unstable, or caregivers face housing and immigration challenges.
This module focuses on practical issues in adoption and guardianship matters encountered in community and family law practice, including the scope of the court’s wardship jurisdiction. Adopting a community-law focused approach, the session examines when guardianship may be sought as a practical solution, including situations where caregivers require legal status to access housing or other forms of support.

events.title: Navigating the Family Office Landscape: A Comparative Study of HK and SG Tax Incentive Schemes
events.venue: RHTLaw Asia LLP 16 Collyer Quay #08-00, Collyer Quay Centre, Singapore 049318
events.outline: This event is organised by RHT Academy Pte. Ltd. This programme provides a practitioners’ overview of the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing family offices in Asia’s two premier wealth hubs. The session examines the methodologies for structuring Family-owned Investment Holding Vehicles (FIHV) in Hong Kong and compares them against the established Section 13O and 13U regimes in Singapore.

events.title: Making the Case for Mediation in ISDS: Internal Advocacy for Government Lawyers and Law Firm Practitioners
events.venue: Asian Civilisation Museum (Ngee Ann Auditorium), 1 Empress PI, Singapore 179555
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore Centre for International Law (NUS-CIL). Building on the 2024 and 2025 partner events, the 2026 CIL–SCW seminar explores how government lawyers and external counsel can champion mediation in Investor-State disputes within their organisations. It addresses common misconceptions, including enforceability, loss of control, and perceived weakness, while presenting mediation as a strategic, credible, outcome-oriented option. Expert panellists will share data and practical advocacy tools for practitioners and government lawyers.

events.title: [WEBINAR] ALB Effective Negotiations for Legal Professionals Masterclass 2026+
events.outline: Designed for professionals who want a structured, repeatable method for achieving better outcomes across commercial and contentious negotiations. Delegates will be introduced to an established framework, the core principles of the Harvard interest-based approach, and seven negotiation behaviours and habits linked to enhanced success. They will apply these concepts through legal simulations, supported by case studies and video analysis, and receive expert feedback and coaching throughout.

events.title: IBA Asia Pacific Arbitration Group Symposium
events.outline: A symposium presented by the IBA Asia Pacific Arbitration Group and supported by the IBA Arbitration Committee and the IBA Asia Pacific Regional Forum. Issues will include geopolitics and sanctions in international arbitration, sovereign immunity and enforcement constraints, ISDS mediation (a new frontier)

events.title: Mediation Through Asian Perspectives: Building Trust in Commercial Dispute Resolution
events.venue: Training Room 701 (Level 7), NTUC Business Centre, One Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018989
events.outline: This panel unites voices from Singapore, China, and Mongolia to examine mediation's role in resolving commercial disputes across Asia. As cross-border business grows, parties need practical, credible dispute resolution that preserves value and relationships. Speakers will discuss how institutions, courts, and practitioners are promoting mediation, what builds party confidence in the process, and how lawyers can foster constructive settlements, while addressing enforceability, standards, and regional cooperation shaping mediation's future.

events.title: [WEBINAR & IN-PERSON] Bridging laws for business — A decade advancing trade, technology and trust
events.outline: This half-day conference celebrates ten years of the Asian Business Law Institute. Among others, it features two panel discussions, one jointly organized with the Hague Conference on Private International Law to commemorate the 11th year of the coming into effect of the HCCH 2005 Choice of Court Convention and the other one dissecting the full lifecycle of cryptoasset dispute resolution in ASEAN, specifically Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

events.title: JLP - Trials (August 2026)+
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: This two-day training module is designed to equip young lawyers with essential and practical skills in preparing for, dealing with and assisting in trial proceedings.

events.title: Singapore IP Week 2026 – Global Forum for Intellectual Property (GFIP)+
events.venue: Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre
events.outline: This event is organised by Intellectual Property Office of Singapore. The theme for Singapore IP Week 2026 is “The Rise of AI: Is It IP as Usual?”. Our anchor conference, GFIP, will examine the intersections of geopolitical divisions, technology, and IP – the opportunities, threats, business and legal strategies. Related topics on IP commercialization, intangible asset valuation, licensing and IP & technology disputes will be covered. The GFIP will be opened by Singapore’s Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs, Mr Edwin Tong, SC.

events.title: Kwa Geok Choo Distinguished Visitors Lecture - The Constitutional Status of the Bomb
events.venue: Yale-NUS Hall, University Town (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: Nuclear disarmament is often dismissed as idealistic, yet nuclear weapons continue to be justified through self-defence and deterrence, and remain deeply embedded in legal and political authority. This lecture explores the bomb as a constitutional artefact that has shaped world order, asking what forms of domination it sustains and why disarmament should be understood not as utopian aspiration, but as a constitutional imperative.

events.title: CML Seminar Series: Charterers and Limitation
events.venue: The Executive Centre Level 22 Ocean Financial Centre 10 Collyer Quay Singapore 049315
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: The interpretation of charterers' rights under the 1976 Limitation of Maritime Claims Convention has been debated in English courts for nearly twenty years, beginning with the 1998 case The Aegean Sea and concluding with the 2025 Supreme Court case The Flaminia (No 2). While English law's position appears established, questions remain about its adequacy and whether other jurisdictions should adopt the English courts' approach.

events.title: Energy in Crisis: Navigating Maritime Disputes Through Artbitration
events.venue: WongPartnership LLP, 12 Marina Blvd, Tower 3, Marina Bay Financial Centre Singapore 018982
events.outline: This event is organised by Singapore Chamber of Maritime Arbitration (SCMA). Global energy instability is reshaping maritime trade. SCMA will examine the Strait of Hormuz crisis, its impact on energy and supply chains, and arbitration's role in resolving related disputes.

events.title: AI Workshop for Legal Professionals (27 August)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Step into the world of artificial intelligence with this practical, in-person workshop designed specifically for legal professionals. Gain foundational skills and the confidence to apply AI in your everyday work—from legal research to drafting and contract analysis. Guided by experienced trainers, you'll explore how to evaluate and use a range of general and legal-specific AI tools effectively and responsibly. Participants will work directly on their own devices with live support, ensuring a hands-on, outcome-focused learning experience.

events.title: Singapore Mediation Lecture and Appreciation Lunch 2026
events.venue: Shangri-La Singapore 22 Orange Grove Road Singapore 258350 Tower Ballroom
events.outline: The Singapore Mediation Lecture (SML) is proudly presented by the Singapore Mediation Centre and Aequitas Law LLP, in collaboration with the Singapore Management University. The lecture has been held annually to enhance the understanding and use of the mediation and ADR processes in managing and resolving disputes. The year’s lecture will be followed by an Appreciation Lunch for the SMC's mediators, adjudicators and dispute resolution advocates. We are pleased to welcome those who wish to meet with like-minded participants and widen individual networks.

events.title: A Menu for IP Mediation – Choices and Options
events.outline: This event is organised by World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) – Arbitration and Mediation Center, Singapore Office. This panel explores how IP and technology disputes are best mediated, examining facilitative, evaluative and transformative approaches, whether parties should choose their preferred style in advance, and where AI may assist. Includes a dedicated ethics segment on neutrality and dual roles.

events.title: International Sports Law Conference 2026
events.outline: The International Sports Law Conference 2026 (Law Society of Singapore) connects sports governance and dispute resolution with global commercial law. Highlights include a Fireside Chat with Singapore's Law Minister and CAS's Director-General on Singapore's role in sports justice, plus sessions on Singapore as Asia's sports gateway and a panel on sports-commercial arbitration synergy. It underscores Singapore's commitment to integrity, rule of law, and advancing global sports administration standards.

events.title: Introduction to International Arbitration
events.venue: Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS), 1 Paya Lebar Link #11-03 PLQ 1, Paya Lebar Quarter, 408533, Singapore
events.outline: This course provides candidates with a foundational understanding of the general principles of International Arbitration, and how it relates to other dispute resolution processes. Candidates will be introduced to the legal framework governing International Arbitration, alongside good practice and procedure. Our lecturers bring hands-on experience in IP and technology-related disputes, offering candidates valuable real-world perspectives throughout the course.

events.title: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 1+
events.venue: Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) The Adelphi, 1 Coleman Street #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 1 is an intensive two-day training programme to learn the foundations of interest-based mediation which focuses on the disputing parties’ interests and encourages a broader range of solutions. You will learn about the nature of conflicts and the most effective techniques to manage them. These fundamental dispute resolution strategies can be applied in diverse situations to manage work relationships within an organisation or with external parties, or to build stronger and more effective teams.

events.title: Certificate in Multi-Jurisdictional Tax and Structures
events.outline: This event is organised by Wealth Management Institute (WMI). This module examines how family offices navigate cross-border tax and regulatory environments. It covers key regimes across major jurisdictions, with a focus on Singapore’s Section 13 incentives, licensing and structuring considerations. Participants explore CRS, FATCA, global minimum tax, and emerging trends, applying insights through practical case studies on family office operations.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 2: Formal Restructuring Options+
events.outline: This module covers two formal restructuring options, namely Schemes of Arrangement (“SOA”) and Judicial Management (“JM”).

events.title: CBFL Seminar Series: Regulating Powerful Businesses: Regulation by Intentional Institutionalism
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: Responsive regulation has shaped regulatory practice for over three decades, yet repeated corporate failures expose its structural limits. This paper argues that the enforcement pyramid is ineffective for powerful institutions because it assumes genuine dialogue and normative engagement. It proposes Intentional Institutionalism, a framework that places corporate culture, leadership accountability, and proactive institutional design at the centre of effective regulation.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Senior Counsel Forum 2026 - Module 4: Conflicts in Relation to Two Existing Clients or Past Clients
events.outline: The Senior Counsel Forum, by the Law Society of Singapore, returns with six modules led by distinguished Senior Counsel. Topics include court submissions, duty to the court, disciplinary processes, conflicts of interest, common ethical scenarios, and English ethics practice. An invaluable opportunity for lawyers to learn best practices in legal ethics, delivered virtually via Zoom.

events.title: JLP - Cross-Examination and Experts+
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Develop essential and practical skills required to cross-examine witnesses in court proceedings, and how to deal with experts and use expert evidence in the course of a dispute.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Community Law Training Programme 2026 - Module 10: Family Violence
events.outline: This module focuses on the practical handling of family violence cases, including applications for Personal Protection Orders (PPOs) and the use of remedies under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) where appropriate. Adopting a community-law focused approach, the session examines how to assess risk, advise clients on available protection, and prepare cases responsibly in time-sensitive situations.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Artificial Intelligence and its Impact on the Legal Profession
events.outline: Does AI mean the end of lawyers? This webinar will address how artificial intelligence is impacting the legal profession – from its effects on the nature of legal practice, AI risk management, legal accountability and the ethical use of AI, as well as how legal roles may evolve in the future. Legal professionals will gain insights from an expert panel that includes representatives from private practice, academia and government, who will examine the current and emerging developments and how lawyers can prepare for AI-driven change.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Formulating Case Theory
events.outline: This session explores the formulation of a compelling case theory in criminal trials — a strategic framework that guides advocates from pre-trial preparation through to closing submissions. Participants will learn how to craft a coherent narrative that aligns with client instructions and ethical obligations, and why establishing a strong case theory early is essential for staying focused, addressing weaknesses, and making sound strategic decisions throughout the trial.

events.title: [NUS Law Bicentennial Lecture on the Rule of Law] Evolving Conceptions of the Rule of Law: The Singapore Experience
events.venue: Yale-NUS College Hall, NUS Law, UTown
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: This address traces the evolution of the rule of law in Singapore, from its procedural foundations to a broader, substantive conception. It examines core principles underpinning stability and commercial credibility, and considers how Singapore adapts to globalisation, fragmentation and AI through enhanced legal coherence, access to justice, therapeutic justice, and international cooperation.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 10: Mastering Sentencing: Key Principles and Evolving Trends
events.outline:
The criminal defence counsel will understand the various factors that are considered by the Courts in the selection and calibration of the appropriate individual and global sentences.
This seminar equips criminal defence counsel with practical insights into sentencing objectives, frameworks, and how recent jurisprudence has shaped their application.

events.title: Public International Law Conference 2026
events.venue: The Law Society of Singapore (Members’ Lounge) ,28 Maxwell Road #01-03, Maxwell Chambers Suites Singapore 069120
events.outline: The post-World War II international order is under unprecedented strain as powerful states increasingly disregard international law, undermine multilateral institutions, and pursue national interests through military and economic force. Organised by the Public and International Law Committee of the Law Society of Singapore, this conference brings together practitioners, academics, and policy experts across four panels to examine what these developments mean for the international rules-based order and for Singapore and the ASEAN region.

events.title: JLP - Client Management
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: Get equipped with essential client management skills, focusing on practical aspects such as AML/KYC issues, client interviews, and dealing with difficult clients.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 11: Mastering Examination: Techniques for Evidence-in-Chief, Cross-Examination, and Re-Examination
events.outline:
Witness testimony is the heart of any trial—shaped through evidence-in-chief, cross-examination, and re-examination. But in a world where truth isn’t always freely offered, skilled examination becomes essential.
In this dynamic session, seasoned practitioners share practical techniques and insights on drawing out compelling, reliable testimony.

events.title: Annual CPD Day 2026 (Part 1): The Inaugural Ethics and Innovation Forum
events.venue: Members' Lounge (The Law Society of Singapore)
events.outline: What does it mean to practise with integrity in an age of AI? Join us for an afternoon CPD programme that brings together the leadership of the Singapore Bar and the architects of its digital future for two focused sessions – offering frank perspectives on where the profession stands today, and what it takes to lead it forward.

events.title: The Singapore Torrens System After Baalman
events.outline: This seminar examines the law of easements under Singapore's Torrens system, highlighting recent developments in implied and court-created easements through landmark cases and expert commentary from contributors to The Singapore Torrens System After Baalman.

events.title: Loss of Profits Fundamentals
events.venue: Room 701, Level 7, NTUC Centre, One Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018989
events.outline: This event is organised by J.S. Held. Getting the quantum wrong can undo an otherwise winning case.  Loss of profits sits at the heart of commercial disputes, including breach of contract, shareholder rows, business interruptions, IP infringement and investment treaty arbitration.  This seminar gives legal practitioners the fundamentals needed to instruct experts effectively, pressure-test opposing calculations, and argue quantum with confidence.

events.title: Legal Innovation Workshop (Sep 2026)+
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This 2-day legal innovation course is designed to provide an analytical excursion of the state of legal innovation in Singapore and the region as well as best practices in legal innovation.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 3: Informal Restructuring Options+
events.outline: This module covers the technical and legal aspects of informal restructuring, i.e., restructuring outside of formal court processes. Participants will learn how to change the composition and/or structure of a distressed debtor company’s assets and liabilities, without the Court’s intervention. The course also reviews both operational restructuring as well as financial restructuring, and how other issues arising from such an exercise need to be managed.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Directors in the Twilight Zone: Duties, Decisions and Liability as Insolvency Approaches
events.outline: This webinar examines how directors’ duties operate as insolvency nears, and when claims for breach of fiduciary duties may be pursued against former directors independently of statutory avoidance or clawback claims. Drawing on the recent decisions of Foo Kian Beng v OP3 International Pte Ltd (in liquidation) and Goh Jin Hian v Inter-Pacific Petroleum Pte Ltd (in liquidation), the speakers will highlight key legal principles and practical indicators of potential breaches of duty.

events.title: Executive Programme in Criminology and Criminal Justice+
events.venue: National University of Singapore (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline:
Criminological research is making fast progress in understanding the causes and prevention of crime, the impact of penal laws and sanctions on behaviour, the prediction of future risk, and the functioning of the criminal justice system.

The course is open to senior legal practitioners, including prosecutors, defence counsel, judges, and other criminal justice professionals/ stakeholders from Singapore.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Ponzi Insolvencies: Clawbacks, Investor Defences and Cross-Border Recovery
events.outline: This event is organised by INSOL International (Asia) Ltd. This webinar examines the legal, commercial and operational challenges arising from modern Ponzi insolvencies, including clawback litigation, investor defences, forensic investigations, asset tracing, digital asset recovery and cross-border recovery strategies. Drawing on recent legal developments and the speakers’ firsthand experience, it also considers the legal, forensic and commercial issues that influence successful recovery outcomes in complex domestic and cross-border frauds.

events.title: CML Seminar Series: Termination for Late Delivery in Charterparties: A Pause for Thought?
events.venue: The Executive Centre Level 22 Ocean Financial Centre 10 Collyer Quay Singapore 049315
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: This seminar examines a hypothetical time charterparty dispute involving late delivery. It considers the conflict between delivery obligations and reasonable diligence, the nature of breach, and the legality of charterer termination. It highlights the innocent party’s decision-making period, shaped by contractual context, urgency, market conditions, performance, and potential prejudice. It also stresses reserving rights and properly framing termination notices, as termination is not automatic.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 12: The "Perfect" Case Theory and the CCDC Process
events.outline: A trial isn’t about throwing every fact and legal argument at the court—it’s about strategy. As solicitors, our role is to distill complex information into a clear, compelling story that shows why our client is not guilty. In this seminar, seasoned advocates share practical insights on crafting a powerful case theory, making the tough calls along the way, and navigating the CCDC process where both sides reveal their strategies.

events.title: [WEBINAR] What Is A "Frozen Conflict" in International Law?
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore, Centre for International Law (NUS CIL). What is a "frozen conflict" in international law? This webinar examines the contested legal meaning of the term, distinguishing frozen conflicts from other contemporary conflicts through a survey of global conflict hotspots. Focusing on the post-Soviet space, Dr. Livia Bonhôte-Enzler explores how these conflicts challenge legal concepts of sovereignty, territorial integrity, self-determination, occupation, and the use of force.

events.title: [WEBINAR] AEICs: The 2026 Paradigm
events.outline: This webinar explores the evolving 2026 paradigm for Affidavits of Evidence in Chief (AEICs) in Singapore civil trials, covering judicial guidance, procedural changes, and technology's growing role. Speakers address best practices for drafting, structuring, and managing factual and expert evidence, integrating electronic material, and avoiding pitfalls. Participants will learn judicial expectations, common AEIC weaknesses, techniques for clarity and persuasiveness, and how to handle cross-examination and submission challenges.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 4: Dispute Resolution+
events.outline: This module is intended to familiarise participants with the different forms of dispute resolution relevant to the restructuring and insolvency contex

events.title: Megaprojects: What Works, What Fails and What’s Next
events.venue: Meeting Room, Level 3, West Tower Marina One, 9 Straits View, Singapore 018937
events.outline: Megaprojects are defined by scale, value & increasingly complex delivery environments. From evolving regulations, compressed delivery timelines to supply chain disruption, stakeholder pressures & shifting commercial realities, project teams operate in more uncertain/challenging conditions. We explore lessons from major projects, how legal frameworks interact with broader aspects, how industry/contractual practices evolve to better manage risk, improve project delivery, achieve better outcomes.

events.title: JLP - Appeals
events.venue: SAL, Stamford 1 & 2, The Adelphi #08-08, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: This training module is designed equip young lawyers with essential and practical skills required to prepare for and handle a civil appeal.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 13: Mastering Oral Advocacy: Preparing to Persuade
events.outline: Advocacy is where preparation meets persuasion. In this session, experienced speakers share practical strategies for crafting compelling oral arguments and navigating courtroom dynamics with confidence and professionalism.

events.title: [WEBINAR] From Principles to Practice: Governing AI and Agentic Systems in Asia’s Fragmented Regulatory Landscape
events.outline: As AI shifts to autonomous agents, legal practitioners face complex compliance risks. This session draws on Europe-Asia comparative jurisprudence to provide a defensible framework for assigning liability, managing cross-border regulatory fragmentation, and engineering accountability by design.

events.title: [WEBINAR] ACRA's Prescribed Anti-Money Laundering Combating the Financing of Terrorism ("AML/CFT") Course
events.outline: This event is organised by Chartered Secretaries Institute Singapore (CSIS). This course intends to equip [Registered Filing Agents (RFAs)] with the knowledge and understanding of anti-money laundering (AML) and counter financing of terrorism (CFT) to enable RFAs to comply with prevailing ACRA and relevant Singapore’s regulatory requirements.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Advocacy in Bail Applications and Closing Arguments
events.outline: Bail affects criminal cases from arrest through appeal. Though straightforward in law, it has practical implications shaping a client's daily experience, mastering both law and practicalities (e.g., bringing a passport to court) boosts perceived competence, while "hiccups" (e.g., unanticipated bail increases with new charges) risk appearing unprofessional. This webinar covers the legal framework, practical scenarios and tips on bail, plus a brief discussion on closing oral arguments at trial.

events.title: [WEBINAR & IN-PERSON] International Commercial Mediation Workshop+
events.venue: Webinar / 137 Amoy Street, Far East Square, #03-06, Singapore 049965
events.outline: This event is organised by Sage Mediation Institute for Leadership Education Pte Ltd. This workshop is designed for those new to mediation or for mediators who wish to enhance their skills for a world following the Singapore Convention on Mediation. Led by seasoned international mediators, you will practice mediating cross-cultural conflicts and try different approaches to de-escalate strong negative emotions. This workshop is a mandatory component of those seeking accreditation as international mediators under the Sage Mediation Institute for Leadership Education.

events.title: Family Office Risk Management and Control
events.venue: Wealth Management Institute, One Marina Boulevard, #16-01, Singapore 018989
events.outline: This event is organsied by Wealth Management Institute Limited. The Family Office Risk Management and Controls Programme equips professionals to navigate complex regulations and tax frameworks in family offices. Covers structures, rationale, and key players. Highlights risks in onboarding, complex structures, cross-border issues, and high-risk jurisdictions. Participants will assess and mitigate these risks through compliance strategies and controls, safeguarding Singapore’s standards in transparency, law, and risk management.

events.title: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 2+
events.venue: Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) The Adelphi, 1 Coleman Street #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This three-day programme conducted by SAL-SMC is highly interactive with role plays and exercises and is taught by experienced faculty. Participants will be able to: Learn advanced concepts in interest-based conflict management Use tried-and-tested mediator strategies and approaches Apply advanced tools for effective communication Recognise the legal and ethical issues in mediation Acquire techniques to overcome impasse Receive insights into drafting settlement agreements.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Building a Professional Brand and Delivering an Impactful Pitch for Legal Professionals (Session 3)
events.outline: This exclusive three-part webinar series is designed to equip legal professionals with the tools, mindset, and strategies to build a compelling personal brand, show up authentically in every interaction, and deliver pitches that win mandates and open doors.

events.title: Advanced Certificate in Law and Technology Module 4: Legal Innovation+
events.outline: In this module, participants will discover the tools and ideas that are driving these big changes. They will also study the principles of innovation and how tech disruption is affecting legal services; from understanding nuances to exploring how they are changing the way lawyers do their jobs.

events.title: [WEBINAR] CLAS Training Programme 2026 - Module 14: Rehabilitation Over Retribution: Alternative Sentencing for Youth and Vulnerable Offenders
events.outline: Ensuring that young and vulnerable offenders have the chance to rehabilitate and reintegrate is a matter of public importance. Often, the most effective justice lies not in incarceration, but in meaningful alternatives that support transformation

events.title: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 1+
events.venue: Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) The Adelphi, 1 Coleman Street #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 1 is an intensive two-day training programme conducted by SAL-SMC to learn the foundations of interest-based mediation which focuses on the disputing parties’ interests and encourages a broader range of solutions. You will learn about the nature of conflicts and the most effective techniques to manage them. These fundamental dispute resolution strategies can be applied in diverse situations to manage work relationships within an organisation or with external parties, or to build stronger and more effective teams.

events.title: Certificate for Family Office Advisors - Advanced+
events.venue: Wealth Management Institute, One Marina Boulevard, #16-01, Singapore 018989
events.outline: This event is organised Wealth Management Institute Limited. by This advanced program goes beyond the basics of Family Offices, focusing on the psychology and motivations of today's UHNW families. It explores opportunities such as impact investing, where affluent clients can align their wealth decisions with societal and environmental values, offering insights into the emerging trends in the field.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 5: Forensics And Investigations+
events.outline: This module provides an insight into the types and motivations of fraud and the obligations of an insolvency practitioner when faced with circumstances involving fraud. Participants will be introduced to a series of investigation methodology and the importance of forensic services in uncovering valuable evidence for the insolvency practitioner.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Day of Conveyancing Highlights 2026 – Day 2
events.outline: The Conveyancing Practice Committee presents its 14th annual "Day of Conveyancing Highlights," held as two half-day webinars covering different topics. Speakers include Leonard Tay (Knight Frank) on residential/commercial market trends, S. Suressh (Harry Elias Partnership) on anti-money laundering, Orson Zhu (SLA) on the upcoming Digital Conveyancing Portal, and Carrie Wong (SLA) on adaptive reuse of State properties - addressing property law, market dynamics, technology, and compliance for practitioners.
